summary: The claim opposes conditionally implementing screen-time limits on E-Rate, arguing that ending E-Rate would place a higher financial burden on taxpayers rather than telecom providers.

claims.argument: If E-Rate support ends, districts would be forced to cover the shortfall and finance internet service and network equipment themselves
claims.evidence_quote: In our district a higher burden of cost would fall on the tax payer and not the companies who fund the E-Rate program.
